historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2019->FY2025 revenue CAGR 2.45% (through-COVID) and Chinese industry traffic +6.4% in H1-2026; book-value and EPS CAGRs are meaningless (losses every year FY2020-25, equity propped by RMB25bn perpetual bonds and a 2022-23 share placement)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR -6.6% vs revenue 5yr +19.0% (COVID-trough base) and EPS negative throughout: equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor. Revenue 3/5yr CAGRs are off the 2020-22 trough and overstate trend growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (post-lease, SBC nil) was negative FY2018-FY2024 on every basis and only +7.3bn in FY2025 on the net-capex basis with a 9.4bn payables inflow; no FCF CAGR is computable. SBC is nil, so reported vs SBC-adjusted divergence does not arise.

scenario_narratives.base: The axes are jet fuel, domestic yield and fleet discipline. Base: the March-2026 Middle East fuel shock (H1 fuel price +36.8%, unhedged) fades through 2027; international routes (33% of passenger revenue, +22% in H1-26) keep compounding under 'Three Flights'; domestic yield stops falling. EBITDA margin recovers from ~19% in FY26 to 24.5%, below the FY2019 peak of 26.6%. Fleet growth (51 introductions in 2026, 49 in 2027, RMB107.6bn of aircraft commitments) keeps net capex at 12-14% of revenue to 2028 before settling at 10.5%. Lease cash falls from 12.3% toward 11% as revenue outgrows a flat ~RMB80bn lease book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fuel normalises fast, international long-haul and premium cabins (first/business revenue +18.8% in H1-26) drive yield, and policy pressure rations domestic capacity so the Big Three stop competing on price. Margins reach 28%, above any year in the record, and C919 economics plus state financing cut fleet cost intensity. Cheap state funding keeps the perpetual-bond and borrowing stack at ~2%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fuel stays high with no hedges, domestic overcapacity keeps yields falling (FY2025 -5%), and the fleet keeps growing because C919 offtake is policy, not a returns decision. Margins plateau at FY2025's ~22%, lease and capex intensity stay high, and the RMB131bn of senior claims plus RMB79bn of leases leave the ordinary equity with nothing. The 87% liability-to-asset ratio means a further shock needs another parent injection, which dilutes H holders.

valuation_philosophy.summary: This is an unlevered owner-FCF DCF under lease treatment B, discounted in CNY and converted to HKD for comparison with the H-share quote. Its core finding is structural. China Eastern has never produced material unlevered free cash flow after aircraft leases and fleet capex, not even in FY2019. The enterprise value a mid-cycle margin path supports does not cover the RMB131bn of borrowings, perpetual bond and NCI that rank ahead of ordinary shareholders, before counting RMB79bn of lease liabilities already charged in the flows. The H-share price is therefore not explained by the cash flows at a commercial cost of capital. It reflects (i) state-subsidised ~2% funding that a WACC model only partly captures, (ii) an implicit parent backstop (CEA Holding perpetuals, its RMB1bn share purchase), and (iii) optionality on a margin cycle above FY2019. Read the scenario values as what the cash flows support, not as a forecast of where the H shares trade.
key_risks_to_valuation: Jet fuel: ~37% of opex in H1-26 with zero hedges; each 10% fuel move is worth roughly 2.5-3pp of EBITDA margin
Domestic yield: Big Three/LCC overcapacity cut yields ~5% in FY2025
Funding cost: ~53% of borrowings float; a return to 4% debt costs removes the leverage spread that equity value rests on
Fleet policy: C919/C909 offtake and RMB107.6bn of commitments are not purely returns-driven
H-share subordination: A/H premium ~58%, and state objectives (routes, emergency operations) rank ahead of minority holders
Model sensitivity: the 12x cap binds in every scenario, so the value is a near-linear function of terminal-year FCF margin, and +/-1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin moves equity by roughly RMB25-30bn
valuation_philosophy.levered_reference_memo: Memo, not a replacement (approximate hand estimate, not engine output). Read at the equity level, base-case terminal FCF (~RMB5.4bn) less after-tax borrowing interest (~RMB1.8bn at 2.2%) and perpetual distributions (~RMB0.7bn), plus net borrowing at constant leverage (~RMB2.8bn), gives ~RMB5.7bn of terminal FCFE. Capitalised at an 11.6% cost of equity and 2.5% growth and discounted 10 years, after the negative FY26-28 equity flows, that is roughly RMB15-25bn of equity, about HKD 0.8-1.3 per share. So even crediting the state-subsidised funding spread, the base case sits well below the HKD 2.4 H-share line. The gap between this memo and the negative unlevered value is what the ~2% policy-priced debt is worth to ordinary holders.
valuation_philosophy.negative_value_note: Base and bear per-share values are negative: modelled enterprise value is below senior claims. Ordinary shares have limited liability, so the practical floor for a holder is zero (or a parent-funded recapitalisation that dilutes H holders), not the negative figure. The weighted value is reported unfloored so that the engine, the workbook and the dashboard sliders all agree.

inputs.share_count_basis: 22,088m A+H shares in issue at 30-Jun-2026 (17,025m A + 5,063m H; H1-2026 interim note 21). No dilutive instruments (note 11). Held FLAT: SBC is nil, and the 2025-26 buybacks (RMB603m FY25, RMB58m H1-26) are immaterial (<0.3% of the count). One intrinsic value per share applies to both classes; it is compared with the H-share quote. A shares (600115.SS) trade ~58% above the H line, which this model does not arbitrate.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 17,148 (OCF 37,941 - gross additions 20,793) - SBC 0 - interest income 0 - lease cash 19,616 (principal 17,577 + lease interest 2,039) under lease treatment (B). On a net-capex basis (gross additions less RMB8,428m pre-delivery-payment refunds on aircraft delivered into finance leases and RMB1,305m disposal proceeds) it was +7,265, flattered by a RMB9.4bn payables inflow. FY2024 on the same net basis: -2.7bn; peak-year FY2019: roughly -3bn. This business has not produced material unlevered post-lease free cash flow in any year in the record.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in the FY2025 cash flow statement or reconciliation (note 44(a)); EquityAwardTaxes nil FY2018-25. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide.
inputs.fx_note: HKD per CNY 1.1721 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X (regularMarketTime 2026-10-10). Cross-check: HKD=X 7.8472 / CNY=X 6.6922 = 1.1726, a 0.04% tie, which confirms rate and direction (CNY value x 1.1721 = HKD). No parity check on the dual listing is possible: A shares (600115.SS, CNY 3.30 = HKD 3.87) carry a structural ~58% AH premium over the H line.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY. Risk-free 1.8% (10Y CGB), ERP 6.5%, levered beta 1.5 -> cost of equity ~11.6%. Pre-tax cost of borrowings 1.70-2.60% (H1-26 note 20; FY25 1.79-2.11%), ~1.65% after 25% tax; perpetual bond to CEA Holding ~3%. At a 35/55/10 equity/debt/perp mix the arithmetic WACC is ~5.3%; 6.5% is used because ~53% of borrowings float and part is USD, so today's state-subsidised 2% funding is not a perpetual given. Identical across scenarios: cyclicality and fuel are charged in the scenario flows, not in the rate (adaptation f). Cap multiple 12x (cyclical) binds over Gordon (25.6x at 6.5%/2.5%) in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full lease cash payment (principal + interest, FY2025 17,577 + 2,039 = 19,616 = 14.0% of revenue; H2-25 12.5%, H1-26 12.2%) is deducted via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (79,017 at 30-Jun-2026: 16,373 current + 62,644 non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY25 27,894 - 14,248 = 13,646 = 9.75%) so cash-tax EBIT does not charge the lease twice. capex_pct_path is NET capex: gross additions less pre-delivery-payment refunds when aircraft are delivered into finance leases and less disposal proceeds (FY25 11,060 = 7.9%; FY24 11,561 = 8.75%; H1-26 11,285 = 15.2% on the fleet ramp).
inputs.perpetual_bond_treatment: RMB25,415m perpetual bond held by CEA Holding (IFRS equity) is treated as DEBT and deducted in equity_bridge; its ~RMB700m/yr distributions are senior to ordinary shareholders and are not in the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI book value 1,287 at 30-Jun-2026 deducted in the bridge; flows are consolidated. NCI is ~3% of equity and its share of results is negative (-237 in H1-26), so the bridge deduction is the single charge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with owner-fcf-adaptations applied: CNY flows / HKD quote, lease treatment B, perpetual bond as debt, NCI in bridge, SBC-zero (band_position null), risk charged once. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). Debt: borrowings 110,222 (50,216 current + 60,006 non-current, includes bonds and super short-term debentures) less cash 5,507 at 30-Jun-2026; restricted deposits (93) ignored. Mid-cycle: FY2026 is a fuel-shock year (H1 jet fuel price +36.8% YoY on Middle East tensions from March 2026; zero hedges outstanding), so FY26 margins are depressed and the scenarios ramp to a mid-cycle EBITDA margin anchored on FY2019 (26.6%, best pre-COVID year) and FY2025 (22.7%). Structural finding: at any WACC/cap combination a reasonable reader would use, the unlevered enterprise value does not cover the RMB131bn of senior claims (borrowings net of cash, perpetual bond, NCI) excluding RMB79bn of leases already in the flows. Equity value here exists only through the state-subsidised ~2% funding spread and an above-2019 margin path; see valuation_philosophy.

bear.narrative: Fuel stays elevated with no hedging, domestic yields keep falling 3-5% a year in a Big Three/LCC share war, and the fleet keeps growing on policy (C919 offtake) regardless of returns; margins plateau at FY2025-like 22%.

base.narrative: Fuel normalises from 2027, international keeps compounding, domestic yields stabilise; EBITDA margin recovers to 24.5% (between FY25 22.7% and FY19 26.6%). Fleet ramp (49 introductions in 2027) keeps net capex elevated through 2028.

bull.narrative: Fuel spike reverses quickly, international long-haul and premium cabins lift yield, domestic overcapacity is rationed under SASAC 'anti-involution' pressure; margins exceed FY2019 at 28% and lease/capex intensity fall as revenue outgrows the fleet.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (up from the 15% default): 87% liabilities/assets, RMB98bn net current liabilities, unhedged fuel in an active shock, and an equity whose value depends on policy-priced funding. Base 50%: margin recovery to below the FY2019 peak is the median outcome for a Big Three carrier. Bull 20% (down from 35%): it needs fuel, domestic pricing discipline and international yield to all go right at once, and requires margins above any year on record.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
